content.snl: def-hyp(list-partial(Type.judge(list-partial(@F, @G), Analysis.PFun), Type.judge(@x, Real)), Analysis.equivInfinitesimal(F, G, x), Logic.and(Analysis.infinitesimal(F, x), Logic.and(Analysis.infinitesimal(G, x), Analysis.funLim(Div.div(F, G), @y, x, $1$))))
content.markdown:
`F ∼ G` at `x₀` iff both are infinitesimals there and their quotient tends to `1`. Note that the quotient is formed in the PFun algebra, so its domain already excludes the zero set of `G` — the usual side condition "`G` is nonzero near `x₀`" is discharged by the carrier rather than stated.

This is an equivalence relation on infinitesimals at a fixed point, and it is the justification for the standard substitution table (`sin u ∼ u`, `√(1+u) − 1 ∼ u/2`, `(1+u)^a − 1 ∼ a·u`). Substitution is valid in factors of a product or quotient, and is *not* valid inside a sum — replacing a summand by an equivalent can destroy the cancellation that determines the answer.
